title: SamGoG: A Sampling-Based Graph-of-Graphs Framework for Imbalanced Graph Classification

problem.claim: Real-world graph classification tasks can suffer from class imbalance and graph size imbalance, which can bias learning and degrade model performance.

gap.claim: Existing methods generally address only one imbalance type or incur high computational costs.

contributions.claim: SamGoG is a sampling-based Graph-of-Graphs learning framework designed to mitigate both class imbalance and graph size imbalance.
The framework constructs multiple Graphs-of-Graphs through importance-based sampling and trains on them sequentially.
The sampling mechanism uses learnable pairwise similarity and adaptive Graph-of-Graphs node degree to enhance edge homophily.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SamGoG achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets.
The authors report up to a 15.66% accuracy improvement and 6.7× training acceleration.
The authors report that SamGoG can integrate with various downstream GNNs for graph classification.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs have been successful in graph classification by capturing structural and feature-based representations.
Real-world graphs exhibit class imbalance and graph size imbalance, which can impair learning.
Existing approaches often handle only one imbalance type or require substantial computation.
SamGoG addresses both imbalance types using importance-based sampling, sequential Graph-of-Graphs training, and adaptive similarity-based construction.
The authors report strong benchmark performance, accuracy gains, and training acceleration.

source_observation.claim: The method targets class imbalance and graph size imbalance together through sampling-based Graph-of-Graphs construction.

interpretation.claim: Jointly modeling multiple imbalance dimensions may address limitations of methods designed for only one imbalance type.

application.claim: For graph classification datasets with both class and graph-size skew, consider a sampling strategy that balances both dimensions before downstream GNN training.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported benchmark datasets or imbalance settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, baselines, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not provide separate results for class imbalance and graph size imbalance.
The abstract does not describe the computational resources or training conditions underlying the reported acceleration.
